I have been farming this land for 50 years. I know every stretch of it. My knees are not what they were, two of my children work in Handan now, so I do not have the hands I once did. I plan carefully to match the work to what I can manage, hiring day labor only at wheat harvest and cotton picking.

My 14 mu splits the way it always has: 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, 6 mu in cotton. The rotation ground is the better-watered plots near the well. Cotton goes on the outer fields where I can move the pump line.

**Wheat:** I sow in mid-October after the maize comes off. I buy the same improved winter wheat variety from the village supply cooperative — it has been consistent here for years and the local station recommends it. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and urea at jointing. I irrigate four times: before sowing to settle the seedbed, at winter dormancy break, jointing, and heading. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide in winter, one aphid-and-rust spray in April. Rotary tillage to work in the maize stubble before sowing.

**Maize:** I plant immediately after wheat harvest in early June, no-till direct seeding. I cannot afford to let the ground sit in July heat. My son-in-law's uncle has the no-till planter and I use it. Hybrid seed, same Zhengdan 958 I have used for years. One herbicide pass, one pest spray mid-season. Three irrigations: at sowing, tasseling, and grain fill if August is dry.

**Cotton:** Ploughed in April, transplanted seedlings in early May. I use the Bt bollworm-resistant improved variety — it has cut my spraying enormously since I switched fifteen years ago. Cotton needs the most water and the most attention. Four irrigations, three pesticide applications mainly for aphids and spider mites since the bollworm is mostly handled by the variety. I apply more potassium than on the grain crops — cotton responds well to it here. Picking runs September and October. I hire two neighbors for the first picking flush.
